segments.title: The big fluffy submarine as a teaching prop
segments.summary: A large submarine plush bought in Japan is both an emotional-support joke and a planned teaching prop for a future year of the submarine.
segments.body: The large submarine plush stays sealed in plastic to protect it on the journey home. It is jokingly promoted to an emotional support submarine, but it also has a planned teaching role in a future year of the submarine. That theme is provisionally about three years away, with next year assigned to destroyers and the current year focused on leadership. The clip connects a comic travel purchase with the channel's sequence of annual teaching themes.

evidence.note: He displays the submarine plush, explains its intended use in future teaching, and identifies the current theme as leadership.

segments.title: Temple searches and closed sites in Japan
segments.summary: A planned memorial visit and unexpected closures on Sarushima Island show how translated names and outdated English information complicate historical travel in Japan.
segments.body: The next day's plan is to visit a memorial, provided the travelers have identified the correct temple. Translated temple names can make the right site difficult to find, while English-language websites may lag behind current conditions. Local people have been quick to explain where to go and what is happening. Sarushima Island, also called Monkey Island, provides the example: places shown as open in a guidebook were closed and appeared to have been so for some time. The closures are disappointing, though they amount to one small part of a much larger trip.

evidence.note: He discusses locating a memorial, outdated English information, and closures on Sarushima Island.
